Composed workflows / outcome systems

Playbooks compose the system.

A playbook coordinates personas, skills, workflows, evidence, artifacts, and quality gates around a meaningful outcome. It is the layer for work that is larger than any one persona or skill.

Personas are the lensesSkills are the capabilitiesPlaybooks are the coordination

On this page

Mental modelCurrent playbookParticipantsShared stateBoundary

How the layers fit

The library stays understandable when each layer has one job. Personas describe who is operating, skills describe what they can do, and playbooks describe how several lenses coordinate.

A playbook is a reusable operating model for an outcome.

It defines stages, participants, handoffs, decision rights, shared state, quality gates, and learning loops. It does not replace the personas or skills it calls.

01 / Primitives

Personas + skills

The reusable material of the system.

  • Personas and operating context
  • Skills and quality signals
  • Resources, tools, and artifacts
02 / Composition

Workflows + stages

The way work is organized and handed off.

  • Foundational, supporting, and edge flows
  • Activities and priorities
  • Decision points and quality gates
03 / Instance

Project + evidence

The specific situation being worked on.

  • Goal, constraints, and current state
  • Evidence and versioned artifacts
  • Decisions, feedback, and learning

Current playbook

The first playbook in this space is an evidence-led job search. It is a concrete example of how the Personas and Skills spaces work together toward one outcome.

Evidence-led job search

Help a person define a realistic target, interpret a role, turn real experience into evidence, create an application packet, prepare for conversations, and learn from the search.

Working model
01 / DEFINEDefine the searchSet role, level, market, constraints, and acceptable adjacencies.
02 / ALIGNCalibrate role + evidenceTranslate the opportunity into outcomes, signals, proof, and gaps.
03 / CREATEMake the packetDraft and review materials for ATS, human, visual, and integrity quality.
04 / LEARNCarry it forwardPrepare conversations, capture feedback, and update the search deliberately.

Participants are coordinated lenses

A playbook does not need to turn every participant into a new composite persona. It can call existing records and give each one a bounded responsibility.

Shared state keeps the playbook coherent

The orchestrator coordinates work through shared objects, not through vague handoffs. Each stage should read from and leave behind a traceable state.

Search brief

Target role, level, market, constraints, timing, and acceptable adjacencies.

Evidence bank

Source experiences, outcomes, artifacts, decisions, metrics, confidence, and gaps.

Artifact versions

Resume, cover letter, portfolio, outreach, interview stories, and review findings.

Decision + learning log

What changed, why it changed, what remains uncertain, and what would change the plan again.

What belongs in a playbook skill?

Yes, eventually. A dedicated playbooks skill should define outcomes, decompose stages, route work to existing personas and skills, manage shared state, enforce quality gates, preserve decision rights, and close the learning loop. It should call persona-research and persona-skills when new lenses or capabilities are needed instead of recreating their methods.
